what: Polarity/threshold verification of the shipped default hook path, requested on review. Concern: D1 report quoted hook threshold 0.95 while the artifact carries 0.05 - a possible inversion. Verified: decide() returns P(can_execute) = 1 - p_ambiguous in head mode; hook asks when P(can_execute) <= 0.95, EXACTLY equivalent to the evaluator convention p_ambiguous >= 0.05 (metrics() uses >=). Previously the hook used strict <, which disagreed with the evaluator only at exact equality p_amb == 0.05 (no val row within 0.048 of the boundary); aligned to <= so the conventions match by construction, not by luck. Frozen val split (n=44) replayed through the hook's decision rule with the shipped artifact: 43/44 correct, FP=1, FN=0 - identical to shared metrics() output and to T5's committed row.

results.semantics: head: ask iff P(can_execute) <= 0.95 <=> p_ambiguous >= 0.05 (evaluator-exact); noul: ask iff P(can_execute) < 0.35 (unchanged)

what: Remove the per-prompt model-load cost, the main dogfooding UX risk named in the README. New plugin/laya_serve.py: a stdlib-only ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1:8735 that loads LAYA + gate_head.json ONCE and serves POST /score {prompt, decider} by reusing promptimize_gate's own loaders (same normalization contract, same artifact - identical scores by construction). The hook tries the server first (PROMPTIMIZE_SERVE_URL, disable with PROMPTIMIZE_SERVE=0) and falls back to the in-process path on ANY error - server is an accelerator, never a requirement; decision log gains via=server|local. laya's own serve.py does not fit: it exposes predict/route for the torch Jev protocol, not the ONNX embeddings the head decider needs, and pulls fastapi/uvicorn/torch deps.

results.score_parity: server 0.9077 vs in-process 0.9077 on the same prompt (identical pipeline)
results.speedup: ~13x per prompt on this hardware; absolute numbers hardware-dependent
results.tests: 167 local tests pass (13 new: serve score dispatch, HTTP surface, hook server-first/fallback, via logging)

verdict: Biggest measured UX cost removed without changing any decision semantics. Server binds localhost only; prompts stay on the machine exactly as in-process.

what: Security review of the D3 long-lived localhost decision server, per maintainer direction: loopback binding alone is not a safety claim. Added (a) shared-token auth: server auto-creates ~/.promptimize/serve_token (0600, or PROMPTIMIZE_SERVE_TOKEN_FILE) and requires the X-Promptimize-Token header on every request (hmac.compare_digest, 401 otherwise); the hook reads the same file and sends the header automatically, so the warm path keeps working with zero setup; (b) Host-header allowlist (127.0.0.1/localhost/[::1], 403 otherwise) blocking DNS-rebinding drive-bys from browser pages pointed at loopback; (c) bounded concurrency: 4 in-flight inferences via a BoundedSemaphore, 503 beyond, so a burst can't pile up ONNX sessions; (d) 500 when the embedded test server has no token configured (fail closed). Existing bounds kept: 1 MB body cap, 100 KB prompt cap. Verified prompt text never reaches stderr access logs.

results.tests: 175 local tests pass (8 new: 401 wrong token, 403 foreign Host via raw http.client, 503 at semaphore cap, prompt-text-never-in-stderr, 500 missing server token config, token file created 0600 and reused, hook sends token header)
results.auth: token required on /score and /healthz alike; hmac constant-time compare
results.rebinding: Host allowlist returns 403 before any body parsing

verdict: Server no longer trusts 'same machine' as a blanket authorization: rebinding pages get 403, other local processes get 401, floods get 503. Residual risks: token is plaintext over loopback (no TLS; acceptable for single-user machine, do not expose the port), the token protects scoring but an attacker with local read access to the user's home dir already has broader access, and ThreadingHTTPServer is stdlib-grade (not audited like a production WSGI server) - mitigated by loopback + token + caps.
next: macOS dogfooding with the hardened server; keep token + host checks if the port is ever re-bound

what: Dogfooding telemetry reader: scripts/summarize_usage.py aggregates ~/.promptimize/usage.jsonl into the numbers the dogfooding decision needs - decision volume, ask rate (recomputed per row from recorded prob/threshold with the decider's own convention: head <=, noul <), server/local via split, decision latency p50/p95/max, blind-spot share, question pipeline (drafted / declined-by-Haiku / skipped-budget / failed) with token totals and estimated cost via the budget ledger's own rate card, errors by type, per-day trend. Two detectors beyond aggregation: any 'prompt' field in the log is a PRIVACY REGRESSION surfaced loudly (count only, text never read), and unknown fields flag schema drift. Malformed lines are counted and skipped. --json for machine reading. Zero network, zero cost.

what: Dataset coverage audit tooling + artifact: scripts/audit_dataset_coverage.py gives per-class prompt-length histograms, asymmetric coverage gaps (covered by one class, empty in the other), long-tail counts at >=200/>=500 chars, ambiguity-type-by-bucket, and --splits per-split coverage; --min-long-ambiguous N is a pre-registration gate any future expanded training set must pass BEFORE retraining. Artifact experiments/d7_coverage_audit.json records the audit on gold + all three frozen splits. Finding: gold ambiguous prompts are short-only (n=210, median 29, max 186 chars, ZERO >=200) while executable prompts reach 295 (31 in 200-299) - the long-ambiguous blind-spot region (P2/P3 0/8, T6 threshold-dead) has literally zero training examples. Train also has a 150-199 asymmetric gap (exec 76, amb 0), and val AND test have zero ambiguous >=200, so the frozen splits cannot measure a long-ambiguous fix: data expansion must extend val/test under the freezing discipline or the fix stays unmeasurable.

results.tests: 236 local tests pass (12 new: bucket edges, histogram/long-tail math, both-direction gap detection, unmeasured buckets, type-by-bucket, malformed-line tolerance, gate pass/fail/threshold/missing-file exit codes, JSON shape)
results.audit: gold ambiguous: 0/210 >=200 (max 186) vs executable 31/210 in 200-299; test-split ambiguous max 186

verdict: The blind spot now has a mechanical data explanation quantified from the gold set itself: the model never saw an ambiguous prompt longer than 186 chars. This is consistent with, not proof of, the fix - that requires the blocked retraining arm. The gate converts T6's 'mitigation must be upstream' into an enforceable pre-registration: no retraining starts on a dataset that still has zero long-ambiguous examples.
